newsitem.title: UK: IRAQ NEARS CRUDE EXPORT TARGET AS GULF SALES RISE.
newsitem.headline: IRAQ NEARS CRUDE EXPORT TARGET AS GULF SALES RISE.

text.p: Iraq is nearing its target of selling 30 million barrels of crude oil by early September, having lined up more customers at its Mina al-Bakr terminal in the Gulf, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Liftings of Basrah Light crude from the terminal should total about 11 million barrels by early next month, according to shipping brokers and traders.
U.S. firm Bayoil has chartered the Jahre Ventura to take 2.65 million barrels and Coastal has chartered the Stena Companion to lift 2.42 million barrels.
The latter has also provisionally fixed the Red Seagull to take a similar quantity of Iraqi crude later this month, the sources said.

Other customers lined up by Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) include U.S. majors Chevron, which is expected to take two million barrels, and Mobil which could take one million barrels to the Far East.
Russian traders Nafta are expected to take a smaller 600,000 barrel-stem loading on August 29.

With a revised Ceyhan loading schedule showing shipments of Kirkuk rising to around 18.5 million barrels, SOMO is on course to reach the target of 30 million barrels set by Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed earlier this week.
